data.title: Endpoint Protection Can Be Disabled Locally
data.summary:
Endpoint protection could be stopped, uninstalled or excluded from scanning by an account
with local administrative rights, and the agent's disappearance produced no alert at the
management console.
data.description:
An endpoint agent that can be switched off by whoever holds local administrator is a
control that protects only against attackers who do not escalate — which is to say, almost
none.

The more consequential failure is silence. Most products support tamper protection and
most consoles can alert on an agent that stops reporting, but neither is enabled by
default in many deployments. The result is that the single most reliable indicator of
compromise — the sensor going quiet — is discarded.

Scan exclusions deserve particular attention. Adding a directory to the exclusion list is
quieter than disabling the agent, leaves the console green, and is rarely reviewed.
data.recommendation:
* Enable tamper protection so that stopping or removing the agent requires a credential
  held in the management console, not on the endpoint.
* Alert on agents that stop reporting, and treat the alert as an incident rather than as
  an inventory discrepancy.
* Review scan exclusions on a schedule and alert on their creation.
* Reduce standing local administrator rights, which is what makes the rest achievable.
data.short_recommendation: Enable tamper protection and alert when an agent stops reporting.
